Package of 5 lessons = up to 5000 words

2.) I will send you a lesson invitation.

pro_course_detail.description:
We'll follow a proven curriculum that will help you advance your English and get you feeling confident as soon as possible! Ideally this syllabus includes 45 minute classes twice a week for ten weeks on your schedule.

These lessons will be tailored to your specific needs.

Curriculum:
Week 1: Pronunciation - common mistakes for your language, review of vowels and consonants 
Week 2: Grammar - differences between common verb tenses
Week 3: Vocabulary - false cognates in your language, expanding vocabulary
Week 4: Conversation - phrasal verbs 
Week 5: Listening - blending
Week 6: Pronunciation - word stress (compound words, schwa)
Week 7: Grammar - prepositions 
Week 8: Vocabulary - root words, switching registers 
Week 9: Conversation - idiomatic expressions 
Week 10: Listening - understanding native speakers

pro_course_detail.title: Improve Your Vocabulary, Accent and Pronunciation with Texts
pro_course_detail.description:
This format is best for those who want to expand their vocabulary and improve their accent.  Many people do not know that accent is more than just your pronunciation; it also includes your intonation patterns, the rhythm of your speech, and the fluency of your speech.  You can have perfect pronunciation but still not sound like a native if you lacking in the other areas of your speech.  

These classes are made to specifically work on accent reduction and building your vocabulary.  To do this, we will use text a digital text which you will read it aloud.  We will focus on specific vowel and consonant sounds , syllable and word stress, and rhythm patters to help you sound more like a native.  

Since we will be using native level content, you will also be exposed to new vocabulary, phrases and sayings.  We will discuss the text and I will help you with any doubts you have.  The texts will be on topics of interest to you so that you can use the vocabulary in your daily life.  The possibilities are endless and include:
- News articles
- Blog posts
- Short stories
- Passages from novels

You can also bring any material that you like, for example a book you are reading, a text for work, a novel for school, etc.  As long as you have the text in a digital format, we can use it in our sessions.

pro_course_detail.title: Beginner's Chichewa for English Speakers
pro_course_detail.description:
Moni nonse! This lesson is for English speakers with no background in Chichewa at all. We will spend time discussing some basic vocabulary and the structure of the language. You will be speaking basic Chichewa in the first lesson. If you choose to continue with more lessons, we will discuss the many interesting facets of Chichewa, like noun classes, locatives, and extremely easy verb tenses.

How do I know Chichewa? I spent almost 3 years in Malawi teaching English to secondary school students. Additionally, my partner is Malawian, a native speaker, so I get a lot of practice in this language. Although I am not a native speaker, I became so fluent that I wrote a 200 page book in the language, which is under consideration for publication in Malawi.

Chichewa is called Chinyanja or Nyanja in Zambia. Chinyanja and Chichewa are generally considered to be the same language but there are some minor differences between them. The variety I speak is Malawian, specifically the dialect from the Kasungu and Lilongwe area, which is considered the standard dialect.

If you have some background in another Bantu language, like Swahili or Zulu, learning Chichewa will be very easy.

For the initial lessons, I follow the same format, though I adapt to each individual students' vocabulary needs depending on why they're learning the language. I have pre-made Quizlet decks with the vocabulary for each lesson I'll share with you, as well as optional post-lesson worksheets. Here is the general structure of lessons we cover:

1. Greetings
2. Pronouns and Verb Tenses
3. Tenses and Tones
4. Questions
5. Intro to Noun Classes (Mu-A Nouns)
6. Chi-Zi Nouns
7. More Verb Tenses
8. Possessives
9. I-Zi Nouns
10. Review Lesson [No Deck]

These lessons tend to be more grammar-heavy than my English lessons (though I can modify that if desired). Post-lesson 10, lessons are more flexible and I include more 'topical' content and themes (i.e. travel, shopping, weddings, funerals, folk tales, etc.)

pro_course_detail.title: American English Pronunciation Workshop
pro_course_detail.description: These lessons are designed to focus explicitly on pronunciation and have you sounding more like a native speaker of American English. Many pronunciation problems can be traced back to the way you pronounce words in your native language. In these lessons, we will discuss the pronunciation rules of your own native language before discussing how to work on the different rules of the English language. We generally also learn the IPA (International Phonetic Alphabet) sounds relevant to English. Because English has so many vowel sounds compared to many other languages, this is often essential in distinguishing between similar-sounding words to non-native speakers (like 'live' and 'leave,' for example). Some people find this lesson type very technical and it can be overwhelming for beginners, but intermediate and advanced learners usually find it helpful.

teacher_info.teaching_style:
My teaching method is as follows:

Step 1: Choose one sound to improve. There are 44 sounds in American English, and the most important to pronounce accurately are: the "R" sound, the "short i", and the "short a".

Step 2: Learn how to create the sound. Know what your tongue and mouth should be doing.

Step 3: Drill the sound with the IPA until it is comfortable.

Step 4: Learn the most common words that use your target sound. 

Step 5: Practice simple sentences using the most common words.

Step 6: Advanced practice (paragraphs, minimal pairs, tongue twisters etc).

Step 7: Test the sound again. Do you still need more practice?

Deep Dive: Analyze all 46 US English phonemes, testing production in initial, medial, and final positions for consonants, both stressed and unstressed for vowels.

pro_course_detail.title: English Speaking and Conversation Class for Professionals: Phrases, Fluency and Idioms.
pro_course_detail.description:
Tired of textbooks? There's a reason for that. How we speak is something different from just good grammar. Did you know that a well-chosen phrase or idiom can make you sound more fluent? It's entirely possible to take your English from good to great with just a little attention to some new ways to phrase things. This course is especially for those times you want to work on your fluency, your pronunciation and usage, and it addresses both business and social environments. Learning happens in a natural and fun way, so you remember and can put your new knowledge into practice immediately.

The method I use in this class is collaborative. You practice real world conversation in a natural and relaxed way, with instruction and feedback/correction given in an ongoing responsive manner. New knowledge is integrated into the class in response to ongoing assessment. 

What this means is that we have a nice, interesting conversation. While we are chatting, I correct your mistakes in writing, and ask further questions to give you a chance to use your new knowledge. As we speak or as we are learning something, I am always doing assessment- finding the patterns in your speech that you can quickly improve to get better spoken English really fast. Quick grammar reviews are given in real time, only as mistakes are made. This is not a traditional grammar class!
